subject: Hosted SLO parity: data asks, test plan, and next steps
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@veridian.ai>, Veridian Procurement <procurement@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted SLO parity — post-call recap and data ask

Alex / procurement team — thanks again for the 45-minute call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope a focused hosted POC to validate p95/p99 parity with your current provider.

Recap (agreed on call):
- Veridian target: tight latency envelope for the user-facing inference API (text generation + streaming for multi-turn chat).
- Primary acceptance criteria: end-to-end p95 and p99 measured from client-to-client (your frontend -> inference -> frontend render).
- Secondary constraints: peak sustained concurrency, streaming chunk SLO, and cold-start behavior.

Data & artifacts we need from you to proceed (small, actionable):
1) Representative traffic profile (single JSON or CSV) covering: request size distribution (tokens), percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests, typical concurrency over 24-hour window, and peak 15-min rate.
2) A small set of recorded end-to-end traces or synthetic replayable traces (we can accept anonymized request IDs).
3) Your current provider baseline: observed client-to-client p95 and p99 (last 2 weeks), and whether those include client-side rendering time or are strictly server-side.

Initial SLO targets we discussed (confirm or correct):
- Target A (conservative): e2e p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 450 ms (including streaming latency contributions for first token).
- Target B (stretch): e2e p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 350 ms.

What Redwood will do after we get the artifacts:
- Produce a compact SLO matrix (attached: slo_matrix_v1.xlsx) mapping test scenarios -> pass/fail thresholds.
- Run a two-phase hosted run: (1) baseline synthetic replay (cache-warm, identical payloads) to measure steady-state p95/p99, (2) mixed-workload run with concurrency shaping to approximate your peak profile.
- Share raw bucketed latency CSVs and per-request traces.

Timeline proposal (we can compress if you prefer):
- We ingest your artifacts by EOD Thu (May 20).
- Redwood runs initial baseline Fri (May 21) and early morning Mon (May 24) for stability checks.
- Review call to go over results and next steps: Tue (May 25) 10:00–10:30 PT.

Immediate ask: please send the traffic profile and the two-week baseline numbers (item 1 & 3 above). If you can drop them in the Doc link or reply with attachments, we’ll begin.

Attachments: slo_matrix_v1.xlsx (contains the proposed test matrix), sample_traffic_profile.json (example schema), latency_samples_20270517.csv (example CSV format).

Thanks — short, clearly scoped POC will get us to an apples-to-apples comparison fast.

—
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@veridian.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Veridian Procurement <procurement@veridian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted SLO parity — post-call recap and data ask

Thanks, Ava — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick answers and attached baseline export.

Quick answers:
- Attached: veridian_traffic_export_20270517.json (anonymized). It includes token-length histogram, a "streaming" boolean flag per request, and per-minute concurrency. Peak 15-min rate: 220 RPS globally (US region ~70% of that).
- Current provider baseline (server-side measured): p95 = 270 ms, p99 = 510 ms (these numbers include model inference + network to our edge, but exclude client render time).
- Streaming: ~28% of requests use streaming. For streaming, ~85% of sessions are using chunked-first-token within 120 ms currently.

We can share a small sample of replay traces (redacted) — attaching latency_samples_20270517.csv. Procurement loop: procurement@veridian.ai is on copy for contract discussion later; for now NDA is already in place.

We’re good with your proposed timeline. Please run the baseline on Fri (21 May) — we’ll be available for a quick sync after results are in.

—
Alex Kim
Lead Product Manager, Conversational AI
alex.kim@veridian.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted SLO parity — internal plan and engineering asks

Looping internal owners — short engineering plan based on Alex’s note and the exported artifacts. High-level approach and owners below:

Plan summary:
1) Validate inputs: confirm schema of veridian_traffic_export_20270517.json and map to our load generator fields (Vivek).
2) Baseline run (Fri 21 May): steady-state run with cache-warm, 15-min sample at median traffic (Ben to coordinate job). Measure server-only and client-approx e2e by adding synthetic client-side latency knob.
3) Mixed workload run (Mon 24 May): follow the spike profile — 220 RPS global peak but focus on US region at ~150 RPS. Include a 20-min sustained peak window.
4) Streaming-specific check: replay the streaming subset (28%) with chunk size matching their frontend (we need to confirm chunk byte sizes; ask below). Measurement: first-token latency distribution and inter-token latency. (Vivek)
5) Cold-starts: run a small set of cold-starts from idle to simulate scale-ups (Marissa).

Engineering assumptions & constraints — callouts for verification:
- Model variant: we'll run both the quantized 8-bit variant and the fp16 variant to see tradeoffs on p99. Prefer to show best-case p95 and p99 across both.
- Warm cache semantics: we will replicate their steady-state profile where prefix KV hits are ~60% (based on token histograms). If that’s off, advise.

Action items (owners):
- Vivek: map traffic export -> load generator + confirm streaming chunk size by EOD Thu.
- Marissa: schedule baseline runs on our hosted cluster Fri 21 May (slot 09:00–12:00 PT) and ensure logs collection and S3 dump.
- Ben: coordinate result packaging and HubSpot update (VER-4821).
- Ava: confirm the review call time with Alex for Tue 25 May 10:00 PT.

If anyone sees missing asks or has a faster slot for runs (we can run overnight), say so. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the timeline above.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@veridian.ai>, Veridian Procurement <procurement@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted SLO parity — post-call recap and data ask

Alex — thanks for the export and numbers. Quick confirmations and one final scheduling note:

1) We will run the baseline Fri 21 May starting 09:00 PT as Ben/Marissa noted. Expect initial CSVs back by end of day Fri and a short summary email.
2) For streaming chunking — Vivek will follow up with a one-line ask if he needs exact chunk byte sizes; otherwise we’ll use the median chunk size from your export.
3) If we succeed on the p95 target but miss on p99 under the same config, our recommendation will be a small model flavor/quantization tweak or an application-side tail mitigation (adaptive retry/fan-out). We’ll include cost delta estimates per scenario.

Proposed review: Tue 25 May 10:00–10:30 PT — confirm and we’ll send an invite. HubSpot record: https://redwood.app/hs/VER-4821

Thanks — looking forward to getting numbers over the finish line.

—
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132
